chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 438: Doumu — The Siming Rises as the Sky Becomes a Yin-Yang Ocean
chapter_meta_description: The Zuowandao summon their Siming, Doumu, turning Shangjing’s reality liquid. Li Huowang nearly breaks under the vision of a god until a familiar eye fixes him in its gaze.
og_title: The Zuowandao Lied to Summon a God — Now It’s Staring at Li Huowang
og_description: Doumu manifests as a living yin-yang ocean that dissolves reality. The zuowandao laugh. Li Huowang bleeds from every orifice. A vertical pupil watches him from the sky.
twitter_title: Doumu Is Here and She Is Not Nice
twitter_description: The Siming of the Zuowandao appears as a universe-eating taiji ocean. First contact with a god in the flesh—and it goes exactly as well as you’d expect.

lore_anchors.definition: The Dipper Mother, a high Daoist deity associated with the Big Dipper, light, and fate. In this novel, she is a Siming whose true form is a vast yin-yang ocean.
An Arbiter of Fate; a class of high-dimensional entities that operate as ontological forces rather than personalities. Seeing one directly causes mental and physical collapse.
A ritual from the Thousand Greats Record that replaces the practitioner’s viscera with parasitic entities, granting them a pseudo-immortal body. Li Huowang is using it to survive.
Zhuge Yuan’s writing tool; by writing characters in the air, he can impose their meaning on reality (e.g., making the canvas move faster with the word “Swift”).
The eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth in Chinese physiognomy. Bleeding from all seven is a classic sign of extreme qi disturbance, supernatural attack, or the body rejecting a divine vision.
Fictional kingdoms in the Dao-Twisted World. The Zuowandao’s illusion-deception was a multi-kingdom operation, pulling energy from all their territories.
A high-rank Zuowandao collective; four beings with cube-shaped heads who orchestrated the Doumu summoning by absorbing the purple light of tricked believers.
The mad cosmic entity that rules the Dao-Twisted World. The Zuowandao claimed it was waking to goad Doumu into appearing, then laughed at their own lie.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Dice lie about the Great Nuo waking up?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They weren’t panicking; they were baiting Doumu into manifesting. The lie was a deliberate provocation to force a response and finish the summoning.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the “white pupil” in the black sea?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The yin-yang ocean of Doumu’s form; the white dot within the black sea is her yang-aspect eye. The golden-masked eye was absorbed into it and is now part of her vision.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the eye stare at Li Huowang specifically?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The golden-masked eye recognized him earlier. Now integrated into Doumu’s perception, the Siming can see him directly—and a Heart-Element anomaly is very hard to ignore.
